questions.q: What is the key difference between data masking and encryption, per this lesson?
options: Masking and encryption are the exact same technique, just with different names
Encrypted data is still the real data, mathematically recoverable with the right key; masked data has no key or permission level that recovers the original value
Encryption is one-way, while masking is always reversible
Masking only applies to numeric fields, while encryption only applies to text fields
questions.explain: Encryption always permits decryption for someone holding the key -- masking is designed so that no one, including a sandbox's most privileged admin, can recover the real value in that environment.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the masking techniques this lesson describes Salesforce's Data Mask product using?
options: Encrypting the field with a reversible key stored in the sandbox
Replacing a value with random characters
Deleting a field's contents entirely
Replacing a value with realistic-looking fake data drawn from the product's own libraries
questions.explain: Data Mask's techniques are realistic-value substitution, random-character replacement, and deletion -- none of them involve a reversible, key-based encryption approach, since masking is designed to be one-way.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say masking has to be re-applied after every sandbox refresh?
options: Because masking automatically wears off after 24 hours regardless of refresh
Because Salesforce requires masking to be reapplied only once per calendar year
Because a refresh replaces the sandbox's contents with a fresh, unmasked copy from production, so previously masked data is overwritten by real data again
Because refreshing a sandbox automatically re-masks it without any action needed
questions.explain: A refresh pulls a fresh copy from production, which is unmasked -- masking isn't a one-time setup step, it's a recurring part of the refresh process itself.

questions.q: What trade-off does this lesson say masking makes?
options: Masking has no trade-offs -- it is a strictly free improvement with no downside
Masking makes an environment permanently unusable for any testing
Masking increases storage costs by a factor of ten
Masking changes real data into fake data, which can occasionally hide a bug that depended on a real value's actual characteristics, in exchange for removing a much larger exposure risk
questions.explain: Masking necessarily sacrifices some data realism -- for example, an oddly formatted real address that broke a validation rule might not exist after masking -- in exchange for removing real customer PII exposure.

questions.q: A team masks their staging sandbox once at creation, then refreshes it monthly without re-masking. A security review later finds real unmasked SSNs there. What caused this?
options: Masking tools are inherently unreliable and randomly fail over time
The sandbox was hacked by an external attacker
Each refresh pulled a fresh, unmasked copy from production, overwriting the earlier masking -- since masking must be reapplied after every refresh, not performed once
SSNs cannot be masked by any Salesforce tool under any circumstances
questions.explain: This is a direct consequence of masking being one-way and refresh-dependent -- refreshing without re-masking reintroduces real, unmasked data every time, exactly the exposure masking exists to prevent.
